faqs.a: It depends on your goal. Emergency funds and short-term goals belong in safe, liquid accounts even at low rates. Money you will not touch for 5+ years usually grows more in investments. This calculator handles the safe-savings side of the plan.

Monthly compounding is the standard for savings accounts, and this calculator uses it. The difference between monthly and daily compounding is tiny - on $10,000 at 5%, daily compounding adds about $2.30 more per year. APY already accounts for compounding frequency, so compare APYs directly.

APY (annual percentage yield) includes the effect of compounding; the plain interest rate does not. A 4.9% rate compounded monthly equals about 5.01% APY. When shopping for accounts, compare the APY - it is the apples-to-apples number.
faqs.q: What is the difference between APR and APY?

faqs.a: Automate it. Set up a transfer the day after payday so the money leaves before you can spend it. People who automate save roughly twice as much as people who rely on willpower, according to behavioral finance research.

savings-calculator.formula:
Monthly rate r = annual rate / 12. Months n = years x 12.
Future value = P x (1 + r)^n + PMT x ((1 + r)^n - 1) / r.
Interest earned = future value - (P + PMT x n).
howTo: Enter your starting balance (use 0 if you are starting from scratch).
Enter how much you will deposit every month.
Enter the annual interest rate your account pays.
Enter how many years you will keep saving.
Read your future balance, total deposits, and the interest earned separately.
keyFacts: Future value = initial deposit grown with interest + all monthly deposits grown with interest.
The formula is: FV = P x (1 + r)^n + PMT x ((1 + r)^n - 1) / r, with r the monthly rate.
Monthly deposits do most of the work early; interest takes over later as the balance grows.

savings-calculator.quickAnswer: Savings grow two ways at once: your deposits add up, and interest compounds on the growing balance. For example, $5,000 upfront plus $200 a month at 5% for 10 years grows to about $39,290 - even though you only deposited $29,000. The extra $10,290 is compound interest doing its quiet work. Raise the monthly deposit and the rate, and the gap between what you put in and what you end with gets dramatically wider.
savings-calculator.tagline: Watch your savings grow with regular deposits and compound interest.
savings-calculator.workedExample:
$5,000 initial, $200/month, 5% annual, 10 years:
1. Monthly rate r = 0.05 / 12 = 0.004167. Months n = 10 x 12 = 120.
2. Growth factor: (1.004167)^120 = about 1.647.
3. Initial grows to: 5,000 x 1.647 = about $8,235.
4. Deposits grow to: 200 x (1.647 - 1) / 0.004167 = 200 x 155.27 = about $31,055.
5. Future balance = 8,235 + 31,055 = about $39,290.
6. You deposited 5,000 + (200 x 120) = $29,000, so about $10,290 is interest.
